title: cache-safe final-layer Mirror-MoE
hypothesis: A final-layer shared matrix plus four per-domain Givens angles will approach independent rank-2 LoRA domain updates with lower bytes, while final-layer-only placement preserves all prompt K/V caches and early-layer placement does not.
mirror_coordinate: four per-domain Givens angles, function R_d^-1 (R_d x W0)
controls: shared base with no domain update
DMoE-style independent rank-2 per-domain LoRA updates
final-layer Mirror view plus per-domain rank-1 private residual
two-layer causal K/V cache probe with final-only vs early+final placement

task.teacher: y=x W0 + x A_d B_d, with independently sampled rank-2 A_d B_d for each domain
task.domain_address: explicit input to all methods; no router is trained; this is disclosed and router bytes/compute are outside scope

development.selection_metric: mean dev MSE across all five prediction methods

cache_probe.success_final_only: max absolute difference across every layer's prefix K and V is exactly 0
cache_probe.multi_layer_control: layer 0 and layer 1 views active; layer 0 K/V unchanged, layer 1 K/V differs by >1e-7

storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: In each 3 fresh worlds Mirror MSE <=1.10x rank-2 LoRA and Mirror bytes <=0.80x rank-2 LoRA; final-only cache difference is exactly zero; early+final control changes layer-1 K/V by >1e-7.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/bytes gate while LoRA control fits, or final-only placement changes any cached K/V; rank-1 residual recovery is reported as a private-state boundary.
boundaries: domain address supplied to all methods
cache audit uses a tiny causal decoder and does not measure production inference
no natural-language quality or throughput claim
